decision: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX. CLAUDE-D303-MF1 is correctly landed and the operative Decision limb is clean, but the repair was executed by deleting the defective sentence from the Decision limb and simultaneously reintroducing it verbatim, as a quoted parenthetical, in the Protocol line of the same entry. Every load-bearing claim was re-derived from primary bytes rather than read back from the draft or the review prompt: eight digests recomputed, three commit ids resolved through git, the file-08 history re-walked from D-177 to HEAD, the D-236 diff read to confirm it did not touch the DR-111 row, the DR-111 status token and both readiness numbers read out of file 08, the frozen subject's leftoverDesign array and basedOn.d293 read from JSON, and both turn-1 reviews' verdicts, counts and exact member sets recomputed. Twenty-eight attacks were run; twenty-seven are refuted and recorded so they are not re-run at turn 3.
decisionRule: CONSENT only if no MUST-FIX and no SHOULD-FIX. One SHOULD-FIX stands, so the verdict is OBJECT.

shouldFix.title: The turn-2 Protocol line's parenthetical replants the exact sentence CLAUDE-D303-MF1 adjudicated as unresolvable, in a 'Lands X (...)' form with zero precedent in 302 adopted entries, and it is redundant with the Decision limb that already records the landing.
shouldFix.claimUnderReview: Lands CLAUDE-D303-MF1 (Decision: delete the sentence "Does not remasure compatibility leftover-join.v2 as current after this successor is recorded.").
shouldFix.whyShouldFix: MF1's holding was not merely that the sentence was misplaced but that its meaning is unresolvable: 'a later reader of the adopted register cannot resolve which was intended.' The repair removed it from the Decision limb and then reintroduced it verbatim, as a quoted string, in the Protocol line of the same entry. On adoption this makes D-303 the first and only entry in COORD containing the composite form, so the register would carry, inside the very entry that removed it, the construction it just found unreadable. It also makes MF1's own load-bearing measurement non-reproducible against the artifact it was measured on. The defect is confined to a non-operative metadata line and the string is explicitly marked as deleted, so the Decision limb is clean and nothing operative is contradicted; that is why this is SHOULD-FIX and not MUST-FIX. But the parenthetical carries no information the entry does not already carry, and its form has no precedent.
shouldFix.repair: Delete the parenthetical, leaving the bare house form 'Lands CLAUDE-D303-MF1.' The landing is already recorded operatively in the Decision limb ('Claude Stage B turn-1 MUST-FIX CLAUDE-D303-MF1 is landed.'), and the finding's full text is retrievable from the review JSON already cited by digest in the same Protocol line. If the coordinator wants the turn-1 draft independently retrievable, cite its frozen digest 425fc5174110a348cbcc55cc8d307267856788dd7767706dd9a680e5438769e0 instead of quoting the sentence; that is precise, is the register's universal citation habit, and does not replant the string.
shouldFix.doesNotRequire: This finding requires no change to the frozen subject, to file 08, to COORD, to any digest, to the warrant citation, to the Decision limb, or to any other sentence of the draft. It does not reopen CLAUDE-D303-MF1, which is correctly landed.
primaryEvidence: The repair itself is correctly executed in the operative text. diff of the turn-1 and turn-2 drafts shows exactly two changed lines; the Decision limb no longer contains 'Does not remasure compatibility leftover-join.v2 as current after this successor is recorded.', and the currency clause 'Frozen compatibility leftover-join.v2 stays frozen; do not record it as current after this successor is recorded.' remains at line 61.

MF1's own measurement is reproducible and still holds against the live register: grep -Eoc 'remasure[sd]* [a-z0-9. -]*as current' docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md returns 0 across all 302 adopted entries.

The same grep against the turn-2 draft returns 1, matching 'remasure compatibility leftover-join.v2 as current' inside the Protocol line. Adopting the draft as written moves the register's count from 0 to 1, and the sole occurrence sits in D-303 itself.

The 'Lands X' construction appears 21 times in COORD and is bare in every one of them (e.g. 'Lands CLAUDE-D241-SF1', 'Lands D254-MF-1', 'Lands D260-T2-MF-1 / MF-2', 'Lands CLAUDE-D284-T2-SF1'). grep -Eo 'Lands [A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9-]* \(' returns 0 matches: the parenthetical form has no precedent.
COORD never quotes deleted text to describe a landed finding: grep -c 'delete the sentence' returns 0.

In both directly comparable turn-2 precedents the landing is recorded in the Decision limb, not a Protocol line, and neither reproduces the repaired text. D-284: 'Lands CLAUDE-D284-T2-SF1. The identifier is named.' D-260: 'Lands D260-T2-MF-1 / MF-2. Lands D260-MF-1 / MF-1.'

The parenthetical is redundant on the draft's own bytes: the Decision limb at line 61 already states 'Claude Stage B turn-1 MUST-FIX CLAUDE-D303-MF1 is landed.', and the Protocol line already cites the turn-1 review at digest 7b8bf0dd43d6d729760769528616d520dff070305e8d0fe70e50ff56e5a23f6a, from which the finding text is retrievable.
